title: Parity of a Constant Function f(x) = 3
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the constant function f(x) = 3 is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Recall the Definitions of Even and Odd Functions
steps.explanation: A function f on a symmetric domain is even if f(-x) = f(x) for all x, and odd if f(-x) = -f(x) for all x.
steps.why: Parity classifies how a function transforms under reflection of its input across x = 0.

steps.title: Evaluate f(-x)
steps.explanation: Because f assigns the constant value 3 to every real input, evaluating at -x yields f(-x) = 3, which equals f(x).
steps.why: A constant function is independent of the sign or value of the input variable x.

steps.title: State the Parity Conclusion
steps.mathExpression: f(-x) = f(x) \implies f(x) = 3 \text{ is an even function}
steps.explanation: Since f(-x) = f(x) for all real numbers x, f(x) = 3 is an even function (its horizontal line graph y = 3 is symmetric across the y-axis).
steps.why: Note that a constant function can be seen as 3*x^0, where the exponent 0 is an even integer.
